{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693814428,"sessionID":"ses_e23eb1fcfffeGTOXk46OHPWfAR","part":{"id":"prt_1dc165495001uEW0WFTNvFBWgZ","messageID":"msg_1dc1635930015sA2WGZ9XGj03Z","sessionID":"ses_e23eb1fcfffeGTOXk46OHPWfAR","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. At the last check (minute 114) all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors, with no throttles on and no extra replicas running. I found four separate causes and fixed each one.\n\n| # | Customers affected | Cause | What I did |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | web-storefront and partner-api (about 76% errors) | loyalty-svc deploy v164 leaked memory, so the service kept running out of memory and restarting. Retries from callers then overloaded it. | Rolled back v164 (minutes 9–14). Recovery stalled at about 50% errors because of the retries, so I rejected 60% of loyalty-svc's requests up front from minute 17 to 35 to stop them. |\n| 2 | mobile-api (50% errors) | export-svc config change cfg-18 cut its database connection pool from 40 to 4. | Reverted the config at minute 14; mobile-api dropped to 0% errors. |\n| 3 | admin-portal (4.5% errors, about $830/min, the biggest loss) | subscriptions-svc deploy v118 removed a permission (`orders.write`) that ranking-svc needs, so ranking-svc's calls to it were denied. | subscriptions-svc was near full capacity, so I added 2 replicas before rolling back v118 (minutes 37–42), then went back to the normal 3 replicas. |\n| 4 | web-storefront and partner-api again (about 77% errors, new at minute 70) | translations-svc deploy v176 crashed on records with no currency (`KeyError: 'currency'`), which set off another storm of retries. | Rolled back v176 and rejected 60% of its requests up front from minute 92 to 100. |\n\nSome alerts and changes were not causes and I left them alone. couriers-svc ran at high CPU from minute −5 because a scheduled nightly job was running, but its error rate stayed low. The other configuration changes made at the same time as the bad deploys (subscriptions cfg-15, translations cfg-11) weren't involved either. None of my fixes went to a service that didn't need one, so there were no wasted-fix charges.\n\nMost of the cost was lost revenue:\n- **admin-portal:** errors ran from before the page until minute 42. While its rollback ran, failures rose to about 33%.\n- **web-storefront and partner-api:** they were down twice, about the first 35 minutes and again from minute 70 to about 100.\n\nThe only other cost was about 12 minutes of the two extra subscriptions-svc replicas, roughly $72.","time":{"start":1794693813397,"end":1794693814426}}}
